tests: Broad academic and professional knowledge across 57 subjects (math, history, law, medicine, etc.).
saturated_note: GPT-4 86.4% (5-shot) in 2023-03; Gemini Ultra 90.0% (CoT@32) in 2023-12 was claimed as first to beat human experts (~89.8%). MMLU-Redux estimates 6.49% of questions contain errors (57% of analysed Virology questions), so the real ceiling is ~93-94%.
sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.03300 https://arxiv.org/pdf/2009.03300 https://github.com/openai/simple-evals https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.08774 https://blog.google/technology/ai/google-gemini-ai https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04127 https://llm-stats.com/benchmarks/mmlu

org: University of Waterloo (TIGER-Lab), with University of Toronto and CMU
tests: Harder, reasoning-heavy successor to MMLU across 14 disciplines, with noisy and trivial questions removed.
best_model: Gemini 3 Pro Preview (High), independent Artificial Analysis run
saturated_note: Top independent score ~90% (AA: Gemini 3 Pro Preview 89.8%, Claude Opus 4.5 Reasoning 89.5%). Self-reported scores reach 89.6% (Qwen3.7 Max, BenchLM) and 90.3% (Sakana Namazu, llm-stats; unconfirmed). BenchLM flags it 'crowded'. Paper-launch best was GPT-4o 72.6%. Label-error ceiling: unconfirmed.

org: New York University (with Cohere and Anthropic)
tests: Graduate-level 'Google-proof' biology, physics and chemistry questions that experts answer well and skilled non-experts with web access fail.
human_baseline: Full set: domain experts 65% (74% discounting clear mistakes), non-experts with web 34%. Diamond subset: experts ~81% / non-experts ~22%, but biased by how Diamond was selected.
saturated_note: o1 (77.3% pass@1) was the first model OpenAI said beat PhD experts, in 2024-09. Gemini 3 Pro hit 91.9% in 2025-11. Epoch AI estimates ~8% of Diamond questions may be invalid, putting the ceiling around 90-92%. Best independent run: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview 95.45% (Vals AI, 2026-09). BenchLM marks it saturated.

org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
tests: Frontier expert-written academic questions across 100+ subjects, built to be hard for the best models at launch.
format: Mixed: ~24% multiple choice, rest exact-match short answer; ~14% multimodal (image + text)
scoring: Accuracy graded by an LLM judge (o3-mini) against the reference answer; calibration error also reported
saturated_note: Launch best: o3-mini (high) 13.4% (2025-01). With tools, the best is Claude Opus 5.5 at 67.7% (2026-09). Aggregators list Opus 5.5 at 64.4% without tools, but Anthropic's page reports only the with-tools number (unconfirmed). FutureHouse estimated ~29% of text-only chem/bio answers conflict with literature; the HLE team's own review found ~18% problematic in a bio/chem subset. So the real ceiling is below 100%.

tests: Grade-school science questions that simple retrieval and word-matching baselines get wrong.
scoring: Accuracy; 1/k credit for a k-way tie that includes the right answer (LLMs usually 25-shot)
saturated_note: GPT-4 hit 96.3% (25-shot) in 2023-03. At launch, the best baseline was 27.1% (random is ~25%). Leaderboard sites claim 97-98% (e.g., o3 98.1% on codesota), but no primary source confirms this.

org: University of Washington and Allen Institute for AI
tests: Commonsense sentence completion: choose the most plausible continuation of an everyday event; wrong endings come from adversarial filtering.
saturated_note: GPT-4 scored 95.3% (10-shot) in 2023-03, matching humans (95.6%). At launch, BERT-Large scored 47.3%. Surge AI found errors in 36% of 300 sampled validation rows. A 2025 audit (arXiv 2504.07825) found ungrammatical text, typos and multiple-correct options.

org: Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington
tests: Winograd-style pronoun/blank resolution needing commonsense, built at scale with adversarial filtering against word-association shortcuts.
saturated_note: Fine-tuned ST-MoE-32B (Google) scored 96.1% on dev in 2022-02, above the 94.0% human score. The best few-shot LLM score is GPT-4 at 87.5% (5-shot, 2023-03), about 93% of human. At launch, the best model scored 79.1%.

tests: Short fact-seeking questions with one indisputable answer, measuring factual recall and whether models abstain instead of hallucinating.
scoring: An LLM grader labels each answer correct / incorrect / not attempted; reports % correct, correct-given-attempted and F-score
human_baseline: No formal human baseline; a third trainer scored 94.4% on 1,000 questions; estimated dataset error rate ~3%
best_model: ERNIE 5.0 (self-reported; paper does not state tool use)
saturated_note: Closed-book (no search) scores remain far from the ceiling. GPT-4.5 scored 62.5% (2025-02) in OpenAI simple-evals; Gemini 3 Pro 69.3% per ERNIE 5.0 report. With search/tools, scores reach 90-97% (e.g., DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp search agent 97.1%), so with retrieval it is effectively saturated. Labs increasingly report SimpleQA Verified, a cleaned version from Google DeepMind (Gemini 3 Pro 72.1%).

tests: Whether a model follows verifiable formatting/content instructions (e.g., 'write over 400 words', 'no commas', 'answer in JSON').
format: Instruction checks: free-text responses checked by deterministic programs
scoring: Accuracy at prompt level and instruction level, each strict and loose (4 metrics)
saturated_note: Llama 3.3 70B reached 92.1% in 2024-12 (earliest 90%+ found). The top score is 95.0% (Qwen3.5-27B, self-reported); many models score 92-95%. At launch, GPT-4 scored 76.9% prompt-level strict. Which metric labs report varies, so scores are not always comparable. Label-error ceiling: unconfirmed.

tests: Synthetic long-context test of whether a model can really use its advertised context window (retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation, QA).
questions: 13 tasks x configurable lengths (paper: 500 examples per task per length, 4K-128K)
scoring: Recall-based accuracy averaged over tasks per context length; 'effective length' = longest length scoring above 85.6% (Llama2-7B at 4K)
saturated_note: Gemini 1.5 Pro averaged 95.8% (94.4% at 128K) in the original paper (2024-04). Top models score ~95-96% at every length up to 128K, so the standard 128K version is near its ceiling. Harder or longer variants are now used to separate models. The 2024-08 date for Jamba-1.5 is its release month, not stated on the RULER page.
